free_tier.stated: Free plan: "Free — $0/month with $1 of monthly usage credits." A new account starts on the Free Trial, "$5 in credits for 30 days", and reverts to Free when the 30 days pass or the $5 is spent; the $1 does not roll over.
free_tier.notes: metered on spend: the USD 1 monthly credit is drawn down by CPU, memory and disk usage billed per second and by outgoing bandwidth billed per GB

per_object_cap.stated: 500 MB maximum volume size on Free, with 1 vCPU and 0.5 GB of RAM per service; the USD 1 a month of credit is the total ceiling

retention.stated: a Trial account's stateful volumes are deleted 30 days after its credits expire unless the account upgrades; the plans FAQ gives 30 days after expiry for the Free or Trial plan; unverified: what counts as expiry for a Free plan
retention.notes: the trial credit covers 30 days; a service stopped for a usage limit, exhausted trial credits or a failed payment keeps its attached volume

egress.terms: usage is billed against the credit balance

interface_detail: the Postgres wire protocol on a private network; a GraphQL API and the railway CLI
chaining: the next step above the Free plan is the Hobby plan at USD 5 a month, which includes USD 5 of usage

limits.value: USD 1 per month of usage after the 30-day trial credit

identity_cost.detail: sign-in with GitHub, Google or an email address; no card for the Free Trial or the Free plan it reverts to; a verified GitHub account gives the Full Trial, otherwise the Limited Trial restricts outbound network access

reliability_note: a Trial account's stateful volumes are deleted 30 days after its credits expire unless the account upgrades

evidence.proved: USD 5 one-time trial credit for 30 days, then USD 1/month non-rollover; 1 vCPU and 0.5 GB per service
the Free plan is $0 a month with $1 of usage credits every month
evidence.quote: Free — $0/month with $1 of monthly usage credits. Up to 1 vCPU / 0.5 GB per service, 1 replica, and 3-day log history.

evidence.proved: the trial needs no card, and the trial reverts to the Free plan without one
evidence.quote: Free Trial — $5 in credits for 30 days to try Railway. No credit card required.

evidence.proved: the login page offers GitHub, Google and an email address
evidence.quote: Log in using email

evidence.proved: the trial falls back to the Free plan with $1 of credit a month, with no payment step named
evidence.quote: After 30 days passes or $5 is spent, the free trial reverts to the [Free](/pricing/plans#plans) plan, which provides $1 of free credit per month.

evidence.proved: a verified GitHub account is what lifts the Limited Trial network restrictions
evidence.quote: If you connect your GitHub account, and we are able to verify it against a set of parameters, you will be on the Full Trial with full network access.

evidence.proved: the plans reference states the Free plan's $1 of free credit per month
evidence.quote: For running small apps with $1 of free credit per month

evidence.proved: the one-time $5 trial reverts to the Free plan, which gives $1 of credit every month
evidence.quote: After 30 days passes or $5 is spent, the free trial reverts to the [Free](/pricing/plans#plans) plan, which provides $1 of free credit per month.

evidence.proved: the Free plan is $0 a month with $1 of usage credits every month
evidence.quote: Free — $0/month with $1 of monthly usage credits. Up to 1 vCPU / 0.5 GB per service, 1 replica, and 3-day log history.

evidence.proved: memory is billed at $10 per GB per month
evidence.quote: | Memory | $0.00000386 per GB/s | $10 per GB |

evidence.proved: platform limits table, Free row: 1 project, 3 services, 1 member, 500 MB maximum volume size, 0 custom domains, 1 concurrent build
a Trial account's stateful volumes are deleted 30 days after its credits expire unless the account upgrades
evidence.quote: Railway deletes stateful volumes created by Trial accounts 30 days after the expiration of your credits. To retain your data, upgrade your account after the Trial period.

evidence.proved: a service stopped for a usage limit, exhausted trial credits or a failed payment keeps its attached volume
evidence.quote: Note: Although Railway will remove your deployment for any of the above reasons, Railway will not remove the [volume](/overview/the-basics#volumes) attached to the service.

evidence.proved: the Hobby plan is $5 a month with $5 of included usage
evidence.quote: | Hobby | $5 | $5/month | 48 vCPU / 48 GB | 6 | 7 days |

evidence.proved: a service with Serverless enabled sleeps between 5 and 10 minutes after its last outbound traffic
evidence.quote: Once a service stops sending packets it is considered inactive after 5 minutes. Inactivity is sampled on an interval rather than measured continuously, so in practice a service sleeps somewhere between 5 and 10 minutes after its last outbound traffic.

evidence.proved: usage is billed on CPU, memory and disk per second and on outgoing bandwidth per GB
evidence.quote: Railway charges per-second for the CPU, memory, and disk your services actually use. No overprovisioning, no idle markup, no surprises. Outgoing bandwidth and object storage are billed per GB.

evidence.proved: the vendor's own post (dated 2025-08-27) says the $1 monthly credit follows the trial every month and is enough to run a small app
evidence.quote: After $5 or 30 days, we will fund your account with $1 of non-rollover credits each month. This is enough to run a small app for free in perpetuity.

evidence.proved: the $1 monthly credit does not roll over
evidence.quote: The credit does not roll over month to month.

evidence.proved: the plans FAQ gives 30 days after expiry as the volume deletion time for the Free or Trial plan
evidence.quote: | Free or Trial plan | 30 days after expiry |

evidence.proved: the pricing FAQ answers yes to trying Railway without a credit card, with a one-time $5 grant
evidence.quote: Can I try Railway without a credit-card? Yes. As a new Railway user, you can sign up for a [Free Trial](/pricing/free-trial). You will receive a one-time grant of $5 to use on resources.

evidence.proved: the login page offers GitHub, Google and email sign-in
evidence.quote: Continue with GitHub Continue with Google Log in using email

evidence.proved: a slept service is woken by traffic from the internet or from another service of the project over the private network
evidence.quote: A service is woken when it receives traffic from the internet or from another service in the same project through the [private network](/networking/private-networking).

evidence.proved: the first request to a slept service may return a 502
evidence.quote: The first request sent to a slept service may return a 502 Bad Gateway response.

notes: a service with Serverless enabled sleeps between 5 and 10 minutes after its last outbound traffic and is woken by inbound traffic from the internet or the project's private network, which can lower the usage billed; the first request to a slept service may return a 502
binding_note: the USD 1 a month of credit runs out first: at USD 10 per GB-month of memory it pays for 0.1 GB-month of memory, before any CPU, volume or egress charge, and it does not roll over
